articles.description:
It all started with a question about cake. IndieWebClub Bangalore had its one-year anniversary on 24 May 2026. After the meetup on 2nd May, I asked Ankur and Tanvi if we could get some cake to celebrate the anniversary. We agreed to it, but a larger idea had taken roots in my mind.
Conception#
On 5th May, I posted in the IWCB admins group chat:
I was wondering if we could do a special meetup on 30th with no agenda and a little anniversary celebration.
Or we could do a small unconference in underline, inviting 10 min talks from the attendees for first few hours and then go somewhere for a cake.
After some back-and-forth, Tanvi and Ankur liked the idea, and thus started the planning for the Special Edition meetup, where we would invite the folks from the IWCB community to present their talks…
articles.title: IndieWebClub Bangalore: Special Edition Meetup, Behind the Scenes

articles.description:
This week note covers the week of 25th–31st May.


Life#
Compared to the week before, I was in good health for most of the last week. I managed to get a lot of work done, and attended three drumming classes as well. Though my playing is still very sloppy, sight reading is slowly coming back to me. I recorded myself playing, and later cringed at the inaccuracies. I’m sad to see how much my skills have declined, but I’m happy to report that I’m progressing much faster than a beginner. I hope that I can finish 3–4 grades worth of learning in a year.
Rains are here to stay, and the weather is much cooler too. Unfortunately, I’m still not in a condition to exercise. I skipped going to the gym last week, and may not be able to this week as well. No running for me either. I didn’t even walk 10000…

This week note covers the week of 18th–24th May.

The Bends

Life#
Last week was a mixed bag. I had some minor health issues that lasted almost through the week. It was annoying and uncomfortable, but I worked through it. My wife and child A also had some cough and cold because of the arrival of rains in Bengaluru. But I am not complaining. The rains have been a lifesaver for me. The temperature has gone down by more than 5 °C and my mood has improved drastically. I know that the rains caused a lot of issues for the traffic last week in Bengaluru, but somehow I managed to narrowly escape them all.
Last week was A’s short summer vacation. After the heat declined, we went around doing small things. On Friday, I took a leave and all three of us went to the Google Ananta office (shown in the p…

articles.description:
Have you ever wanted to reread that old article posted by your favourite author on their website? Do you use feed readers and wish that some great posts from your friends magically reappear in your inbox so that you can remember the good old days? Do you want to use your feed reader as sort of a space-repetition tool? Well then, feed-repeat is for you.
I have just released the version 1.0 of feed-repeat, a small tool that does only one thing: it takes some posts from the RSS/Atom feeds you configure and puts them in a new Atom feed that you can subscribe to in your feed reader. That’s all.
I made feed-repeat for myself. I wanted a tool to send me old blogposts written by my favourite authors so that I could enjoy them again, but also not be overwhelmed by a wall of hundreds of unread old p…
articles.title: Announcing feed-repeat v1.0

articles.description:
This week note covers the week of 11th–17th May.

Life#
Last week was sort of a rebound to the weeks before, that is to say, it wasn’t a great week. A was sick the entire week and I was worried sick. I made the mistake of having some coffee on Tuesday (only 10ml espresso though), and then going to the gym. My body just couldn’t take them together, and I messed up my sleep completely.
Then to combat the sleepiness next day I drank more coffee, and it made me lose even more sleep. The lack of sleep, the worry, and the exhaustion from the gym session completely ruined my days. I was too sleepy and too tired to do anything other than most essential tasks. I had to take Friday off just to recover.
After sleeping for 10 hours on the Friday night, I felt refreshed, so I went for a short run on Sa…

articles.description:
This week note covers the week of 4th–10th May.

Paris? Paris!

Life#
After a gap of three weeks, I finally felt recovered enough last week to be more physically active. I was able to hit the gym twice, and also go for a run after a break of a whole month. I also walked 20kms. It was nice to feel the energy back in my body.




The downside was the soreness and exhaustion I felt most of the time. I barely could do anything else outside work. I wasted a lot of time staring at the screens before I finally got so fed up on Saturday that I went for a long walk. It was just before the rains and the weather was amazing. The walk refreshed me and brought me out of the zombieness.
I seem to be going through some sort of SAD spell, most likely due to the summer heat making me unable to do fun thing…

articles.description:
In recent months I've heard of several teams with an interesting policy:
each pull request should be no more than a few files, and no more than a
certain number of lines (say 500). And do just one thing and do it well. And
be easy for a human to review. And be fully tested by the test suite.
All those are good requirements, right? Surely this is quality software
engineering.
And often, the results are good. Sure, splitting a single 6000-line feature
or fix into twelve 500-line PRs is more work, but each of those PRs is
surely easier to review. And you can git bisect them when there's a bug! And
maybe revert the individual change that broke something.
...and also cause 12x as many context switches for your
reviewers as they
review each one sequentially.1 But that's just the cost of
software…
articles.title: The software industry: annealing, but wrong

A preprint of this blog can be found here: PDF, DOI (Groot Koerkamp 2026).
1 Abstract
 
 
 Link to heading
 

Motivation.
In recent years, there has been a renewed interest in the search for low density
minimizer schemes. These schemes take a window of \(w\) consecutive \(k\)-mers,
and sample one of them: the smallest under some specific order.
Schemes such as the mod-minimizer provide a low density (fraction of sampled \(k\)-mers) when
\(k \gg w\), while schemes such as the greedy minimizer work well for explicit
small parameters roughly in the regime \(k \leq 2w\), for \(k\) and \(w\) up
to \(15\) or so.
articles.title: The anti-lexicographic SUS-anchor: a near-optimal k=1 sampling scheme
